utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecution versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see everybody is here. If there are problems with interpretation, please let us know. Prosecution, same team as yesterday, Mr. Thayer and Mr. McCloskey. I see the witness already in the courtroom, and I take that to mean that there are no preliminaries; correct? I also wish to thank the Defence teams for filing the estimated time for cross-examination for the next batch of witnesses, which is extremely helpful, fully understanding that the situation remains fluid and can change at any time, requiring less or more time as necessary. I think, all in all, we are doing fine, but we will step in, in no soft manner, if we gather that there is an unnecessary or unreasonable, unacceptable, usage of time. But so far so good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer started examining you yesterday. We only ran the direct for about half an hour. We will continue this morning, sir. Good morning to you. Hopefully we will finish with the examination-in-chief, hopefully, and then we will move to the cross-examinations. Mr. Haynes, is there a reason why you are trying to hide from me?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: There must have been a very short person sitting in that chair before me and it's rather too high.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified yesterday at page 4084, lines 9 to 12, that your separate police formation was a company, and let's use the abbreviation of "PJP" from now on to refer to your separate police units, if we may. You testified that your PJP company comprised approximately 100 to 120 men, and that they were drawn mostly from the surrounding area. Do you recall that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may move into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please, therefore, pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you just described your arrival in the Snagovo area. Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber how your operation actually got under way, and what you did, what you saw, what you encountered for the first couple of days, first few days, of the operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, when we spent the night, and then the next day the company commander came to us there and he informed us where we would be going and what we would be doing. And we were there until the evening. We went back in the evening to the place where we spent the night, the first night. That's where we spent every night. We would go a couple of kilometres away, and at the end of the day we would return to that starting position.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Witness, would you describe the terrain you found yourself in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The terrain was hilly. It was a mountainous area. It was above the town, and there were mountains already there, villages, and so on. It wasn't civilised. There are woods mostly and mountains in relation to the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So physically what would you do during the day in these woods and mountains?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, before that, I'd like to hear what he heard from his company commander. He testified that, "the next day the company commander came to us there and he informed us where we would be going and what we would be doing." What did he say in specific terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He told us, "Well, here we are. We arrived. We're going -- actually, you will be going to mop up terrain, mop up terrain. I personally did not hear him say "killing." We received orders at the station before we left. Perhaps he did say it, but I didn't hear that. There were more than a hundred people there, and you cannot hear everything, perhaps, and I was not in a good position to be able to hear that. We were sent there, and we went to search the terrain and everything, mopping up, searching. In those first few days, we didn't encounter any resistance. We didn't. And then on the fourth or the fifth day, there were some people running across. Muslim people were arriving at the line in order to go and link up with Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, when you refer to your company commander, what was the company commander's name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. He has already given us his name before in private session, so I think we need to go back to private session to have him answer your question. Unless you think it's safe, but I don't think it's safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Given the region it covers, but out of an abundance of caution, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you clarify with the witness what the word in Serbian for "mopping up" is, as the witness has said?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Serbian the term is "ciscenje terena osvajanje."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, prior to the time that you personally saw any Muslims or encounter any Muslims during this operation, what, if anything, did you hear going on in the woods around you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could hear, but not so near that you could hear everything, but you could hear shouting, moaning, something like that. I didn't see anything. It was far off in the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you hear anyone being called out to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what side, do you mean? There were calls to surrender from this side, from the Serb side, using loudspeakers and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you hear any gunfire or shooting of any kind during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but in the distance, somewhere over there. It wasn't so far and it wasn't so near. It was a couple of hundred metres off, 2 to 300 metres, all depending on the terrain where you were. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this period of time, Witness, did you also discover any bodies in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I passed by a couple of corpses that were a meter away, and I wasn't even paying attention to the rest. Well, you could smell the corpses. It was summer, so you could smell that. And you would run away from something like that. If the wind was blowing in that direction, you would try to bypass the bodies as much as you can so that you didn't smell the stench. So I didn't see so many corpses, but I did see what I saw with my own eyes. What I said about the bodies stinking and things like that, yes, depending on the direction of the wind.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Among the bodies that you did see, sir, were they men only or did they also include women and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men who had remained until that breakthrough of theirs. I saw them, and there were children, too. I didn't go up to actually look, because it was a corpse, decomposing corpse, and it was summer and it was a pretty strong stench. It was a very unpleasant smell, so you would just run away from that, go somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, you just testified that there were children or dead children among the bodies that you saw. How was it that you knew there were children among the corpses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well… Looking from a distance, one would say that it was a child. I didn't go up personally to the corpse, but when you looked at it from a distance, you could see that it was a child, looking at it from far off. There were bloody traces on clothes; there was footwear. I also saw some of that. I saw that. I passed next to things like that, and I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, at some point did you, in fact, encounter some Muslims who were still alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I did not, until this group that came out in front of me personally. Before then I didn't see anyone alive, until I saw this group that came up right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please describe for the Trial Chamber what occurred when you saw this group.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that the group came out of the woods in front of me some 5, 6, to 10 metres in front of me, let's say, and they were shouting, "Don't shoot." But this group that I was with from the (redacted) (redacted) nobody fired from the group. They surrendered to us, but then when they did that, all the others from the other stations gathered around to see who was there, what was going on, and then somebody came up, I don't know who he is or what he is, he had some sort of band tied around his head. We were all dressed in the same way, in the uniforms of the olive-drab colour. I can say that the man took his pistol out, and before he took his pistol out, three of them came out. I hid the youngest one behind me and I protected him while this man took out his pistol, and the other two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Could you just look at line 8 on page 27. We're in private session, and the witness has mentioned the origin of -- we are in open session, and the witness has mentioned -- I think we need to redact that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was trying to catch his attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So, Madam Registrar, please redact the words -- the last three words in that line, line 8, and the first word in line 9. And I think we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let's back up for a moment. When you first saw these Muslims, can you tell the Trial Chamber, were they men, women, children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were men. They were men ranging from 35 to 40 years of age. That's what they looked like when you looked at them. One of them was 16, a child at the time, whom I hid behind me to stop him from getting killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, I just want to caution you again not to mention specific names while we're in open session. Let me ask you: How many Muslim males did you personally see -- recall seeing with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw three. I saw three from my own angle, from the position that I was in at the time. I saw three. It all just happened very suddenly, quickly, and from what I remember, I saw three of them from my angle of vision.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you told by fellow PJP officers a different number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw three from my angle. In their statements that they provided, they said it was four. Maybe he saw four. I saw three. This is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can you describe the general appearance of these males when you encountered them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They looked exhausted, as if they had slept in the woods, in the fields. In that sense they weren't at home. They slept wherever they found themselves, in the woods, on the road, in the fields, wherever they happened to be. That's what they looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that things seemed to be happening fast to you, that a crowd gathered, others came over. Can you describe what happened after the males surrendered? What happened to them physically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened was that the youngest one amongst them, the one who was 16 years old, he -- I personally hid him behind me, and the others were killed on the spot, a couple of metres, 5, 6, or 10 metres, away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not those individuals were searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were searched, but there was nothing. They didn't have any bags with them. Maybe a rucksack, a plain rucksack, that didn't have anything special in it that would warrant a search. They didn't have anything on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When these other officers began to gather, do you recall any discussion or anything that was said by the officers after they had learned that you had captured these Muslim men and boy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether anything was said, how. We didn't capture them. They gave themselves up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see -- and you described to some degree already, but did you see who did the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see, but that was the first time I saw that man. I have no idea who it is. I even thought that he was from the Bijeljina station, but he wasn't. Later, there were stories, and it was said that it was some man from Zvornik. I wouldn't recognise him. This all happened in 5 to 10 minutes, and then there is no more trace of anything after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see where these men were shot? Not the location but where in their bodies they were shot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the head area. I turned my head slightly so that I wouldn't look, but it was in the head area. Then after they fell, I didn't turn around any more and I didn't look at those people who were killed. We left immediately. I took away the child from that place. I turned his head also so that he doesn't have to look. I mean, it was traumatic for me - I was younger then - and I'm sure it was traumatic for him who was only 16 at the time. We left that terrain, and we didn't return again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe the reaction that this boy had to the shooting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. The boy was frightened, traumatised. You know how it is when everything is disrupted because of fear. There were all sorts of things going on with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you restrain the boy at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-107 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We restrained him immediately for his safety and security, so that he wouldn't run off and escape and so that he would stay alive, because when he saw all of that and he wasn't killed immediately, he probably thought that then he would stay alive. So he was restrained with handcuffs, and that was safer for him. He probably saw, since he wasn't killed immediately, that he would survive. I couldn't do it when he just turned up in front of me, and I wouldn't allow anyone else to do it, at least as far as he was concerned, because he was the youngest. He was a child. I don't know if anyone could do something like that. Just speaking for myself, I couldn't even kill a child or an older person, in any event, in a case when there is no firing on both sides. When a person surrenders by themselves, I don't see any reason to kill them or anyone else. But the line of separation is something else, where there is shooting on both sides. But in this case, where people surrender on their own and are begging for their lives, why would you do anything like that, take away what they're asking for? At least that's what I thought then at that time, that he shouldn't be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move into a different area that's in private session. I see we're approaching the break, so I would suggest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a 30-minute break, because of the redaction, starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, you may proceed. Please remember that we are in private session, and I got the impression that you wanted to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That we are in open session and you wanted to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When we finished, we were in private session. Do you want to proceed in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go back to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not accustomed to staying in private session for that long, so I get lost sometimes. Is it you, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. We'll need to stop at 1.30 or a little bit before that, if necessary -- if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: With your leave, what I'm going to try and do is deal with one topic, because I'm conscious of the fact that the Court will be constituted differently on Monday, apart from anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And with the best will in the world, I think it's going to be largely in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let me explain to the witness who you are. Mr. Haynes is lead counsel appearing for General Pandurevic in this case, and he will be cross-examining you first from the various Defence teams. He will continue -- he will start today and continue on Monday. Mr. Haynes, let's go into private session --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- I take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will continue on Monday morning, if I remember well. Monday morning. In the meantime, the same caution I gave you yesterday: You are not to communicate with -- or allow anyone to communicate with you on the subject matter of your testimony. Have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.32 p.m.,
